subject: Clarify billing behavior for microbursts, prefix caching, and rounding
messages:
From: Marta Rios <marta.rios@aerologix.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aerologix.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on microburst billing and prefix caching for pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aerologix is excited about the latency numbers. Before we move to a pilot, procurement needs a clear picture of how small, frequent inference calls will be billed. A few specific asks: 

- If we send lots of 1–4 token generation calls (microbursts), how are they rounded or bucketed?
- We plan to use heavy prefix reuse (same user prompt header + small variable tail). How does prefix/KV caching reduce billable tokens?
- For long-context calls where we stream exchanges, how do you apply minimums/rounding across streaming fragments?

I attached a small CSV with our projected daily microburst pattern and a couple of sample requests. If you can give a few concrete examples (input tokens -> billable tokens) that procurement can review, that would speed the SOW.

Best,
Marta
Procurement Lead, Aerologix

Attachment: aerologix_usage_sample_aug2026.csv (CSV)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Rios <marta.rios@aerologix.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on microburst billing and prefix caching for pilot

Hi Marta — thanks for the sample, it was useful. Looping in Logan and Tessa to align on pricing and minimums.

Short answers up front, then a few worked examples below. I can follow up with a one-page matrix (attached) and a sample invoice showing identical math.

High level:
- Quantum (rounding) for generation calls: billable generation tokens are rounded up to the nearest 10-token quantum for the Pilot SKU. So a 3-token generation is billed as 10 tokens.
- Prefix/KV caching: repeated identical prefixes within a conversation are credited automatically; we do not bill for cached prefix tokens on subsequent requests within the same session/window.
- Streaming fragments: we evaluate billable tokens per logical request (application-level call). If you stream the same logical request in N fragments, we combine token accounting for that request before applying rounding/minimums.

Worked examples (Pilot SKU):
1) Microburst: user sends a 2-token generation (no context). Billable = ceil(2 / 10) * 10 = 10 tokens charged.
2) Prefix reuse: initial request has 100 prefix tokens + 20 generation tokens -> billable = (100 + 20) rounded to quantum for generation; on later requests in same session that reuse the 100-token prefix, prefix tokens are free (credited) and you only pay for the new generations (again rounded to quantum).
3) Streaming: if you stream a 400-token context in two fragments as part of a single logical request, we aggregate the tokens to 400 before applying rounding/minimums.

Caveats and opt-outs: we can pilot a smaller quantum for high-volume microburst customers (e.g., 5-token quantum) on a contract commitment. Also available: a session-based minimum (30 tokens/session) instead of per-call quantum for use cases where you have many tiny calls but predictable active-session patterns.

See attached: redwood_billing_matrix_v2.xlsx and sample_invoice_aero.pdf — both show the same math.

Next steps: if you and procurement are comfortable, Logan can draft a 3-month pilot SOW with the 5-token quantum option and a 30% pilot discount we typically offer for first-quarter commitments.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_billing_matrix_v2.xlsx (Excel), sample_invoice_aero.pdf (PDF)

Kimberly / Tessa — quick internal note on negotiation posture for Aerologix:

- Offer structure: 3-month pilot, 30% off list for the pilot period, include a 5-token quantum for generation (to address their microburst economics) conditioned on a $35k minimum commit for the quarter.
- Minimums: waive the session minimum for month 1 to remove friction for their engineering alpha. Month 2–3 reinstate session minimum (30 tokens/session) but factor into the commit math so it doesn't hit them unexpectedly.
- Legal/Finance ask: we should document rounding rules in the SOW appendix and include one worked invoice example for transparency (Tessa, can you produce a sample invoice that shows both the 10-token and 5-token quantum scenarios?).

If Aerologix pushes back on the commit, propose a telemetry-based guardrail: if daily microburst volume > X, auto-transition them to 10-token quantum and pro-rate. That keeps us protected on unit economics.

I'll take the lead on SOW draft once Tessa confirms sample invoice. Sergio — can you own the pilot ops checklist and make sure we have KV-cache TTL settings consistent with our crediting assumptions?

Thanks,
Logan
Director, Strategic Accounts

Hi Marta — following up with a concise summary and the proposed pilot terms so procurement has everything in one place. Quoting your original ask below for context.

On Mon, Aug 17, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marta Rios <marta.rios@aerologix.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo last week — Aerologix is excited about the latency numbers. Before we move to a pilot, procurement needs a clear picture of how small, frequent inference calls will be billed.

Summary of agreed behavior (pilot):
- Default quantum: 10-token quantum for generation calls. All generation usage is rounded up to the nearest 10 tokens. Example: 1–10 tokens -> 10 billed; 11–20 -> 20 billed.
- Pilot exception: 5-token quantum available for the three-month pilot if Aerologix signs the $35k Q commitment. Example: 3 tokens -> billed as 5 tokens under pilot exception.
- Prefix/KV caching credit: identical prefixes within a session are credited on subsequent requests. You are only billed for new tokens (generations + non-cached context).
- Streaming/fragment aggregation: tokens are accounted per logical request. Streaming fragments of the same request are aggregated before rounding.
- Session minimum: 30 tokens/session reinstated after month 1 (month 1 waived). We will reflect session minimum math in the SOW appendix so it is explicit.

Attached: redwood_billing_matrix_v2.xlsx (examples comparing 5/10-token quantum), sample_invoice_aero.pdf (worked invoice), Aerologix usage sample you provided.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, Procurement signs the attached SOW (DocuSign link) and we kick off a 30–45 minute on-boarding call.
2) Tessa will share the sample invoice and billing appendix for the SOW.

If you want one more worked scenario using your exact CSV rows, tell me which row to use and I'll run it through billing math and return a single-line invoice example.

Best,
Kimberly
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
